column4: Barrito reads as "grano/barro en la cara" (pimple) or as the trumpeting sound an elephant makes (barritar), not "little mud"; "fanguito" (from fango) keeps the mud sense without the false friend.
糯米 is glutinous/sticky RICE specifically; "Pegajosito" drops "rice" entirely and just says "sticky", losing the referent.

Seta is the Iberian/Spain term for mushroom; the app already uses the neutral LatAm "hongo" in n017 (Hongito), so the little-mushroom variant should follow the same root and the established "-ín" pattern used elsewhere (Piedrita/Piedrín, Frijolito/Frijolín).

Empanadita names a specific, very different LatAm food (a baked/fried pastry turnover), not a boiled/steamed jiaozi dumpling; "bolita rellena" (little stuffed ball) matches the shape without the false food association, and fits the "Bolita de X" family used for n015/n034/etc.
Frijolito Verde reads as the green string bean (ejote/judía verde) to most Spanish speakers, not the mung bean; "frijol mungo" is the standard term and avoids that mix-up.
Habita names the fava bean (haba), a different legume from edamame (young soybean); "edamame" is now a recognized loanword in Spanish and keeps the reference accurate.

呆呆 (dozy/spacy) already sits next to n046 Bobito and n047 Tontito, two near-synonyms for "silly"; three near-identical glosses in a row are hard for a learner to tell apart, and "lerdito" (slow/dreamy) better matches "dozy" specifically. (Also, if kept, standard spelling is "zonzo/zonzito", not "sonso".)
Gorgorito means a vocal trill/warble (as in singing), not a liquid/stomach gurgle; "gorgotito" (from gorgoteo) matches "Gurgle".

This glosses the English name "Shadow" instead of the Chinese: 小黑 means "little black (one)", the classic affectionate name for a dark-furred pet — "Negrito" is the natural, very common Spanish equivalent.
